draft.title: Ecosystem functioning
card: An ecosystem is the living things in an area (plants, animals, microbes) and the non-living things they depend on, such as soil, water, air and sunlight.
Energy flows one way through an ecosystem. Producers such as plants capture sunlight, and consumers get energy by eating them. At each step some energy is lost as heat.
Nutrients and water cycle. Decomposers break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil, where plants take them up again. Water moves between air, land, living things and oceans.
A food web shows who eats whom. It maps the paths that energy and nutrients take between living parts of the ecosystem.
draft.remember: Energy flows through an ecosystem and is lost as heat. Nutrients and water are used again.

a.q: Which statement best describes how energy and nutrients move in an ecosystem?
opts: Energy flows through and is lost, but nutrients are reused
Energy and nutrients both cycle round and round forever
Nutrients flow one way, but energy is reused by decomposers
Energy and nutrients both enter from the sun and are lost
a.why: Energy comes from the sun, passes along the food web and leaves as heat, so it cannot be reused. Nutrients are returned to the soil by decomposers and taken up again. The second option is tempting, but energy does not cycle.
a.clue: Which one is lost as heat at each step?

b.q: A fire kills the grass in a paddock in Victoria, and dead plant matter piles up on the soil. Which process returns nutrients from this matter so new grass can grow?
opts: Decomposers breaking down the dead matter
Producers capturing sunlight through photosynthesis
Consumers passing energy along the food web
Heat loss at each step of the food web
b.why: Decomposers break down dead matter and release nutrients into the soil, where new plants take them up. Producers capture sunlight, which is energy, not a return of nutrients. That makes the second option tempting but wrong for this question.
b.clue: Which group works on dead matter?

a.best: Energy flows through and is lost, but nutrients are reused

b.best: Decomposers breaking down the dead matter

problems.detail: Why (a) calls 'the second option' tempting but wrong. The options are shuffled, and as shown the second option is the correct answer, so this line contradicts the right answer. Explanations should name options by content, not by position.

Why (b) says 'the second option' is tempting but wrong. As shown, the second option is the correct answer (decomposers), and the producers option it seems to mean is first. Position references break under random order and mislead students.
For Year 12 HSC this is very easy. The stem stresses 'dead plant matter', and the clue 'Which group works on dead matter?' points straight to decomposers, so it barely tests understanding.

Nutrients flow one way, but energy is reused by decomposers

a.why: Energy comes from the sun, passes along the food web and leaves as heat, so it cannot be reused. Nutrients are returned to the soil by decomposers and taken up again. The option saying both cycle forever is tempting, but energy does not cycle.

b.q: Each year a landholder in NSW clears every fallen leaf and dead log from a patch of bushland. Over many years, what is most likely to happen?
opts: Soil nutrients fall, so plants grow more slowly
Plants capture less sunlight, so energy input falls
Less energy is lost as heat, so plants grow faster
Nutrients rise, as decomposers have less to break down
b.why: Dead leaves and logs are what decomposers break down to return nutrients to the soil. Removing them takes those nutrients out of the cycle, so the soil slowly gets poorer. The option about sunlight is tempting, but clearing dead matter from the ground does not change the energy plants capture from the sun.
b.clue: Think about what the removed material would have become.
